main_text.p: crafliores ac denfiores pel- aëris obfiftunt, hinc ratio pendet, cûr Solis refractio (vt loquitur D.Straufs p.205.) feu potius radiorum Solarium ad fupremum atmosphæræ refractorum atque reflexorum vibratio prope Terram mane fortior fit quàm vefperi? cur horæ ab ortu Solis (potius ab exordio crepufculi matutini) ad meridiem longiores, quàm à meridie ad Solis occasum (feu potius ad finem crepufculi vefperti- ni:) mane namque, cæteris paribus, defæcatior aër eft, vefpertinis exhalationibus, quæ aërem Terræ vicinorem obnubilabant, in Terram deciduis: Cæterùm Solis imago vefperi diutius fupra Horizontem apparet, Soleipfo infra Horizontem exiftente, quàm mane, ob refractionem radiorum vefpertino tempore majorem; unde potius à meridie ad Solis occasum apparentem horæ longiores, quàm ab ortu Solis apparente ad meridiem. Ex allatis

page.notes: Scan is a page from a 17th-century book; the top line "PVLVERE" is the running head. Some words are faint or partly obscured by a fold and ink show-through; the transcription of the first lines and the words "crafliores", "vefpertinis" and "fupra" is uncertain. Section numbers and the bottom "allatis" word are at the foot of the text.
